# Appeal of Denial — Lower Back Disc Surgery / Decompression (CPT 63030)

**Member:** Morgan Foster
**Member ID:** W162894592
**Plan:** Ambetter (Commercial/ACA), Illinois
**Denial date:** 2026-08-23
**Reference number:** POC-F4C641ED8B-99591

---

Dear Ambetter Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT 63030), as stated in the notice dated 2026-08-23, reference number POC-F4C641ED8B-99591. My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to reconsider its decision.

This request is governed by the plan's own policy: **Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures (CP.MP.114)** (https://www.ambetterhealth.com/content/dam/centene/ambetteril/clinical-policies/CP.MP.114.pdf). I believe my medical records meet the criteria set out in that policy, and I am asking the plan to review the specific criteria below against the evidence in my file.

## How my records match the plan's own criteria

The policy states that discectomy is medically necessary when meeting all of the following:

**1. Diagnosis of herniated lumbar disc.**
The plan's policy requires "Dia gnosis of herniated lumbar disc." My MRI of the lumbar spine, dated 2026-06-26, shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion, which is a herniated lumbar disc.

**2. Nerve root compression confirmed by imaging.**
The policy requires "Ne rve root compression confirmed by imaging and one of the following:". The same MRI documents severe right lateral recess stenosis with compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.

**3. Radiculopathy with sensory deficit and failed conservative therapy.**
The policy describes "Radiculopathy with sensory deficit as evidenced by pain, parasthesias or numbness in a nerve root distribution, and member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative ther apy including all the following:". My records document radicular pain extending into my right calf, along with positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. This matches the sensory-deficit radiculopathy described in the policy.

The conservative-therapy elements required under this section of the policy, and how my records address each one, are:

- **"a) ≥ four wee ks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program..."** — I completed 12 weeks (18 visits) of supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, from 2026-04-24 to 2026-07-17, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- **"b) ≥ four weeks activity modification;"** — [Please confirm with Dr. Reyes's office whether activity modification of at least four weeks is documented separately in the clinical notes, as this was not clearly itemized in the summary provided to me.]
- **"1) Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) or acetaminophen ≥ thre e weeks unless contraindicated or not tolerated;"** — I took NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, which exceeds the three-week minimum.
- **"2) Epidural steroid inj ection;"** — I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-17, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.

**4. Timeframe.**
The policy requires that conservative therapy occur "within the last year." My physical therapy, medication trial, and epidural steroid injection all occurred within the past year, alongside 24 months of progressive low back pain that has not been relieved by rest.

## My function and current condition

I am currently unable to stand for more than 10 minutes at a time because of the pain, and I continue to have radicular pain into my right calf despite completing the conservative measures described above. I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, and I do not smoke.

## What I am asking

Based on the plan's own policy criteria and the medical evidence summarized above, I am asking Ambetter to reverse the denial and approve coverage for CPT 63030 as recommended by my surgeon. If any part of my file is incomplete — particularly documentation of activity modification — I would appreciate the opportunity to supplement it, and I have asked Dr. Reyes's office to provide any additional records that may be needed.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-19, though I recognize the date on my denial letter is authoritative. I am submitting this appeal through ambetterhealth.com (selecting Illinois and using the state's appeal/grievance form), and I am also sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial notice. I can be reached at the number on my member ID card if any additional information is needed.

Thank you for reconsidering my request.

Sincerely,

Morgan Foster
Member ID: W162894592
[Date]
[Contact phone number]
[Signature]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
